title: Adaptive kernel routing and KV-scheduler tweaks for Mistral/Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning)
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads showed inconsistent latency/throughput tradeoffs across model families (Mistral, Qwen, Llama variants) when using a single kernel selection and KV cache routing policy. This PR introduces an adaptive kernel routing layer and a lightweight KV-scheduler that chooses sharding and prefetch priorities per model and request workload, plus targeted GQA/MQA tuning knobs. The goals are: reduce p50/p95 latency variance, increase sustained throughput for mixed-sequence traffic, and avoid tail regressions when switching model variants. Summary of changes (single-line condensed): implement model profiles for kernel selection and quantization-aware algorithms; add KV-scheduler with per-route priority and prefetch window; continuous-batching changes to respect model affinity and early-flush heuristics; small Llama-specific attention correction for 8-bit MQA flows; Qwen memory layout workaround to avoid kernel thrash on long-context streams; add microbench harness + regression tests + docs updates. Checklist: 1) Perf harness and baseline numbers included 2) Unit tests for scheduler logic 3) Integration canary on perf-canary passed 4) Added release notes and console docs 5) Backwards-compatible config defaults. Commits summary: 1) "model-profiles: add adaptive kernel routing and profile schema" 2) "runtime: KV-scheduler implementation and tests" 3) "batcher: affinity and early-flush integration" 4) "mistral: 8-bit attention edge-case fix" 5) "qwen: continuous-kernel fallback for long context" 6) "docs: runtime tuning guide and release notes" Changed areas (high-level file list): runtime/kernel_router.cpp; runtime/kernel_selector.h; runtime/kv_scheduler.{cc,h}; runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp; models/mistral/attention_fixes.cpp; models/qwen/kernel_fallback.cpp; perf/bench/kv_sched_harness.py; docs/runtime/optimizations.md; tests/runtime/test_kv_scheduler.py. Small illustrative snippets (kept minimal): added selection score calculation in kernel_router.cpp to prefer quantization-aware kernels for MQA flows; KV-scheduler uses LRU-backed prefetch window with a per-model weight. Tests and CI: initial CI run hit an intermittent GPU smoke failure in integration/gpu-smoke (nvidia-alloc-timeout), retried and passed; full perf-canary run showed 6-12% median latency reduction for Mistral-7B workloads (p50 down 8% median), and 18-24% increase in sustained tokens/sec for mixed short+long sequences on Qwen-14B when MQA profile enabled. Llama 2-13B 8-bit flows showed a 4% p95 improvement after the attention edge-case fix. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout for 2 weeks on dedicated cluster subset, followed by staged enablement per customer for private deployments; follow-up ENG task to instrument model-profile telemetry and auto-tune heuristics. Backwards compatibility: default kernel_router policy remains legacy until feature flag is enabled; config knobs documented. Release notes: performance: adaptive kernel routing and KV-scheduler reduce latency variance and improve throughput across Mistral/Qwen/LLM families; fixes: Mistral 8-bit attention correctness; notes: may improve or change token cost estimates due to different kernel selection. Related tickets: ENG-7684 (runtime perf initiative), ENG-7721 (KV scheduling design).

release_notes: Adaptive kernel routing: per-model profiles choose quantization-aware kernels to improve MQA/GQA throughput.
KV-scheduler: reduces tail latency by prefetching hot KV shards and applying per-route priority.
Mistral fix: correctness edge-case for 8-bit attention flows.
Qwen: kernel fallback for long-context to avoid repeated kernel re-compilation thrash.
